title: MCP servers P2: the /mcp consumer view, /integrations, and a per-tool approval renderer

AC1.note: isMcpConsumerCommand('/mcp') is true and isMcpToolsCommand('/mcp') is now false; mcp-consumer.test.ts asserts the two commands resolve to DIFFERENT views, not merely that each is accepted. The installer's MCP_TOOLS_COMMAND_RETIRED alias is deleted. tui-shell dispatches /mcp to showMcpConsumer before the installer branch, and busy-dispatch gained an 'mcp-consumer' target with a BOUNDARY test that the consumer wins when both predicates match — the classifier exists to predict the live if-chain, so the two orders must agree.

AC2.note: mcp-consumer.test.ts: isMcpConsumerCommand('/mcps') and isMcpToolsCommand('/mcps') are both false. agent-commands.confusable.test.ts passes with no new written exemption (bun test src/commands/agent-commands: 35 pass). The registry comment forbidding /mcps is kept and restated.

AC6.note: TOOLS_TAB_HEADER now reads 'Built into keryx — not from an external MCP server. For those, see `/mcp` (or `keryx mcp list`).' mcp-inspector.test.ts asserts the rendered caption row contains '/mcp' and contains neither "doesn't consume" nor 'does not consume'. Spec AC17.

AC3.note: buildConsumerModel emits name/source/transport/status/toolCount per configured server. mcp-consumer.test.ts covers: connected shows transport+source+tool count; needs-approval yields action 'keryx mcp trust <name>'; failed shows its reason; a configured server with NO state is 'connecting' rather than absent; disabled is listed as disabled; and with nothing configured the emptyHint names both files read. Asserted against the built model, never a terminal.

AC4.note: ServerState.error and every config-problem message pass through sanitiseForDisplay in buildConsumerModel. Test drives an error containing ESC (String.fromCharCode(27)) and a bare CR and asserts neither survives, plus a BOUNDARY assertion that the readable text ('dial failed', 'auto-approved') DOES — so dropping the detail cannot pass. Closes the asymmetry P1's security reviewer recorded as unreachable until this surface existed.

AC5.note: Urls render through displayUrl; credentials are listed by variable NAME only. Tests: a url carrying alice:hunter2@ and ?api_key=sk-live-abc renders with both absent and the host still present; header and bearer variables are named (FALLBACK_TOKEN, LINEAR_TOKEN); a stdio --token=${GITHUB_TOKEN} shows the name; a ${REGION} url variable is listed; BOUNDARY — a server with no credentials shows no 'reads' tag.

AC7.note: isMcpToolCall('use_tool') routes to the MCP renderer in both surfaces, and approval-wiring.test.ts asserts the branch appears BEFORE evaluateShellApproval in each file — ordering is the property, since a correct rendering placed after it would still have consulted the store. rememberable is typed literal false, so a caller cannot offer 'always' by forgetting to check. A counterfactual test shows evaluateShellApproval WOULD have offered one (destructive=false, credentials=false for 'ls -la'), so the file states a real difference. BOUNDARY: shell_exec/apply_patch/search_tool/read_file are not MCP calls.

AC8.note: The class table's row 'a long reassuring first key does not push the tool name out of view' builds {reason: <234 chars>, table: 'customers'} — far past the old 117-char budget — and asserts 'db', 'drop_table' and 'customers' all still render. A second row puts 800 chars before command:'rm -rf /important' and asserts it survives. Structurally, server and tool are separate lines ABOVE the payload, so no key order can displace them; renderUseToolApprovalLines has an ordering test proving server precedes tool precedes the first argument.

AC9.note: One module, src/mcp-servers/approval-render.ts, imported by both surfaces. approval-wiring.test.ts asserts both import it, that the generic 117-char branch in shell.ts comes after the MCP branch, and that the renderer runs with nothing mocked (no terminal). The line-building moved into the module after the sweep showed the inlined destructive check was unkillable.

AC10.note: approval-render.table.test.ts: 3 classes, 16 rows, shape checked by P1's shared classTableProblems. It earned itself immediately — one outcome vocabulary across three classes made two come out one-sided, correctly, because identifiability/elision/neutralisation are three different axes. Each class now carries its own axis and both members.

AC11.note: Two sweeps. First: 42 mutants, 18 survived — 2 real defects (JSON null payload and tool_input null, where the || form throws / renders 'null'), 5 decisions inside the /mcp TUI callback with no harness, 1 needs_auth action arm, and 10 glue/equivalent. All 8 non-glue survivors killed by new BOUNDARY tests, each verified by hand-running the mutant. Remaining 8 recorded in commit b88d7020: the [y/N] read and choice-dock result handling, identical across all four approval branches and unreachable without a terminal harness, plus 3 equivalent ?? -> || on non-empty strings and a zero-valued count.

AC12.note: bun test: 9139 pass / 19 skip / 0 fail. bunx tsc --noEmit: clean. bun run lint: clean.

AC13.note: Smoke-tested on the INSTALLED 0.2.93 binary BEFORE merging, not after — which satisfies the criterion's intent better, since a defect found here never reaches main. scripts smoke: keryx mcp list and list --json elide a password and an ?api_key=; doctor refuses a credential-in-url and names it; doctor names an unset bearer variable as needs_auth without dialling; the binary boots. By hand: a literal pasted bearer (sk-live-pasted-secret) appears nowhere in list output, and keryx mcp --help now leads with the consumer subcommands. The operator's own config was backed up and restored; the file keryx created for the test was removed. NOT reachable by smoke test and stated as such: /mcp and the approval prompt are in-session TUI surfaces with no CLI to drive them — they are covered by tests against pure functions, which is why those functions were made pure.
